items.text:
He knew everyone on the island. Whenever his car stopped, half a dozen voices ____ (178) _____ shout out his name. Policemen, agricultural labourers of low social status and priests waved and smiled  ____  (179)  ____  he  passed;  everyone  greeted  him  as  a brother. They respected his honesty, and belligerence, and above all, they adored his typically Greek scorn and fearlessness when dealing  with  any  _____  (180)____  of  Governmental red tape. On arrival,  two  of  our  cases  containing  linen  and other things had been  ______  (181)____  by  the  Customs  on  the  curious  ground that they were merchandise. So, when we moved out to the villa and  the  problem  of  bed  linen  arose,  Mother  told  Spiro  ______ (182) _____ our cases in the Customs and asked for his advice.
- Q.178.
- (a) can            (b) should       (c) would         (d) could
- Q.179.
(a) nor            (b) so                (c) as             (d) thus
- Q.180.

The (188)______ life in Kashmir was drawing to its end after three (189)______ months. Miss Joan was leaving a week earlier than Mrs.  Rhodes,  and  about  two  days  before  she  left,  I  took  her alone to the hotel  for  dinner.  We  walked  to  the  hotel  in (190)______  silence,  a  silence  so heavy that I could (191)______ breathe.  The  hotel  seemed  to  be  far  away  and  yet  not  far (192)______.
Q.188. (a) tonetic   (b) romantic   (c) biquadratic   (d) mucolytic
Q.189. (a) anonymous   (b) analogous   (c) jealous   (d) glorious
- Q.190.
(a) direct           (b) perfect          (c) select     (d) slack
- Q.191.
- (a) hardly          (b) loudly           (c) gladly      (d) gradually
- Q.192.
- (a) thorough     (b) overweigh   (c) clough    (d) enough

items.text:
In  terms  of  technical  difficulty,  Nanga  Parbat,  the world's ninth (193)_____  peak,  competes  with  K2.  The  first  (194)_____ to the summit follows  a  narrow  ridge.  The  15,000-foot  Rupal  Face,  a single wall of rock and ice, is located on the mountain's southern side. Climbers have dubbed the Nanga Parbat, which (195)______ as  'naked  mountain',  'Killer  Mountain'.  This  gives  Annapurna  a (196)______ of 32%, making it the most statistically dangerous of the world's 8,000-metre peaks. It is an avalanche-prone area with some  technical  difficulty.  Climbers'  misery  is  (197)_______  by insufficient  local  support,  in  addition  to  unpredictable  weather and inaccessibility.
Q.193.
- (a) deepest    (b) lengthiest    (c) highest    (d) fattest
- Q.194.
(a) rise           (b) ascent          (c) lift            (d) launch
- Q.195. (a) transliterates

items.text: To  forgive  an  injury is often  (198)_______  to  be  a  sign  of weakness;  it  is  really  a  sign  of  (199)_____  .  It  is  easy  to  allow oneself to be carried away by resentment and hate into an act of (200)______  but  it  takes  a  strong  character  to  restrain  those natural passions. The man who (201)___ an injury proves himself to  be  the  superior  of  the  man  who  wronged him, and puts the wrong-doer to shame. (202)___ may even turn a foe into a friend.
